Introduction Here we will discuss about GitHub that:
What is GitHub? Why we use GitHub? How to use GitHub? What is GitHub? Before we know about GitHub, it is important to know about Git and Open-Source Projects.
1. Git Git is a version control system that tracks any changes a developer makes to their projects, enabling them to revert certain changes they made or return to a past version of their project.
2. Open-Source Project Open-Source Projects are, in simple terms, software projects that have their source code open and available to use by anyone.
Here comes GitHub’s role. GitHub is a web-based Git or version control repository and Internet hosting service.
GitHub is the best place to share code with friends, co-workers, classmates, and complete strangers. Over a million people use GitHub to build amazing things together.
Why we use GitHub? GitHub allows developers to host their open-source projects on an online repository to be available for everyone, and uses Git to allow developers to track their projects and collaborate on other people’s projects.
Today GitHub is used by millions of developers and has succeeded in building a huge community where millions of developers from all over the world collaborate on open-source projects.
How to use GitHub? Search for GitHub in your browser.
After doing so, click on the first link.
Enter your Username or email address and password, then click on Sign in.
After that, a dashboard of GitHub will appear.
From here, you can upload files in your repositories and find other users’ repositories as well.
